subject: math

objective.text: Draw and label a bar graph to represent data. Relate the count scale to the number line.

explanations.title: A graph looks like a tape diagram
explanations.text: Turn a picture graph on its side. It looks like a tape diagram. The bars show the same amounts as the circles.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: It looks just like a tape diagram!)

explanations.title: Longest and shortest bar
explanations.text: The category with the most has the tallest bar. The category with the least has the shortest bar.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: The category with the most is the tallest)

explanations.title: Turn the graph
explanations.text: A graph can be vertical or horizontal. The data stay the same when you turn it.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (We can change the position of the graph... the data stay the same)

explanations.title: Bar graph
explanations.text: A bar graph shows each category as a bar. It has a title, labels and a scale. The scale tells how much each box equals.

explanations.title: Scale is a number line
explanations.text: The scale is like a number line or a ruler. If we count by ones, each box equals one.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: It's a number line!)

explanations.title: Same data, three ways
explanations.text: The same data can go in a table, a picture graph or a bar graph. The title stays the same.

examples.title: Bird bar
examples.text: The scale counts by ones. Each box equals one. Color four boxes for four birds.

examples.title: Jose and Laura
examples.text: Jose read 8 books. Laura read 5 books. The bars show 8 is longer than 5. The difference is 3.

questions.text: An animal table shows birds 6, fish 5, mammals 11 and reptiles 3. How many more birds than reptiles are there?
Use the same table. How many more birds and mammals are there than fish and reptiles?
How many fewer reptiles and fish than mammals are there?
A second animal table shows birds 7, fish 12, mammals 8 and reptiles 6. How many more fish than reptiles are there?
Use the same table. How many more fish and mammals are there than birds and reptiles?
A pet shop table shows fur 12, feathers 9, shells 8 and scales 11. How many more animals have fur than shells?
Which pair has more, fur and feathers or shells and scales? How many more?

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
